decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Economic activity and employment have continued to recover but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its description of the economy to reflect that activity and employment have continued to recover rather than merely picking up.

changes.quote: Weaker demand and earlier declines in oil prices have been holding down consumer price inflation.
changes.explanation: The language shifted to describe oil price declines as earlier events rather than ongoing significantly lower factors.

changes.quote: Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.
changes.explanation: Financial conditions are now described as remaining accommodative instead of having improved in recent months.

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.
changes.explanation: The list of voters was updated to include Robert S. Kaplan and Mary C. Daly.

changes.quote: Ms. Daly voted as an alternate member at this meeting.
changes.explanation: A new note was added to record that Ms. Daly voted as an alternate member.

tone_quotes.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world.
The ongoing public health crisis will continue to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term.
The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.58% APR costs about $60.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 0.79% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.81% would rise by about $1.60 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.9%, and employers added an average of 1,068k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.2% over the past year (October 2020); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 34.9% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.95%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.62% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve intends to keep its benchmark interest rate at zero until maximum employment and 2 percent inflation are achieved. As an educational forecast model, the next meeting projects a 53% chance of a hold and a 47% chance of a cut.
